questions.prompt: Which of the following transactions is subject to value-added tax?

choices.text: Sale of fertilizer, seeds including their ingredients.
Sale of goods, services or importation, the annual gross receipts do not exceed the VAT threshold.

questions.rationale: Sale of petroleum products is subject to VAT. Fertilizers and seeds are VAT-exempt under specific provisions of the NIRC; sales by agricultural contract growers are exempt; and taxpayers whose annual gross receipts do not exceed the VAT threshold are exempt from VAT.
questions.canonicalConcept: VAT-exempt transactions vs VAT-subject transactions under the NIRC

questions.prompt: Which of the following transactions is subject to zero-rated value-added tax?

choices.text: Services rendered to persons engaged in international shipping or air transport operations.
Services rendered by banks, non-bank financial intermediaries.
Generation, transmission and distribution of electricity.
Services rendered by professionals such as CPAs, Physicians and Lawyers.

questions.rationale: Services rendered to persons engaged in international shipping or air transport operations are subject to zero-rated VAT under Section 108(B) of the NIRC. Banking services, electricity distribution, and professional services are either VAT-exempt or subject to 12% VAT, not zero-rated.
questions.canonicalConcept: Zero-rated VAT transactions under Section 108(B) of the NIRC

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not exempt from VAT?

choices.text: Services rendered by school duly accredited by Philippine Government.
Sale of digital or electronic books as well as Journals covered by UNESCO.
Sale of medicines for cancer, mental illness, tuberculosis and kidney disease.
Sale of capital equipment for COVID-19 response.

questions.rationale: Accredited educational services, digital books and journals under UNESCO agreements, and specific medicines for critical illnesses are VAT-exempt under the NIRC. The sale of capital equipment for COVID-19 response is not categorically VAT-exempt unless covered by specific PEZA or special law incentives.
questions.canonicalConcept: VAT-exempt goods and services under the NIRC and special laws

questions.prompt: Which of the following transactions is subject to zero-rated value-added tax?

choices.text: Services by regional or area headquarters of multi-national corporations.
Sale to Philippine Economic Zone Authority.
Sales by non-agricultural, non-electric, non-credit cooperatives.
Importation of professional instruments and implements by settlers in the Philippines.

questions.rationale: Sales to PEZA-registered economic zones are considered export sales and are subject to zero-rated VAT under Section 106(A)(2)(a) of the NIRC. Regional headquarters services are VAT-exempt, cooperative sales may be exempt depending on type, and importation by settlers has specific conditional exemptions.
questions.canonicalConcept: Zero-rated VAT on sales to ecozones and PEZA-registered entities

questions.prompt: Which of the following businesses is allowed a presumptive input value-added tax?
questions.rationale: Under Revenue Regulations, manufacturers of packed noodles (along with sardines and mackerel in tin cans) are allowed presumptive input VAT. Manufacturers of canned goods, packed juices, and dried fish are not covered by the presumptive input VAT provisions.
questions.canonicalConcept: Presumptive input VAT allowed under Revenue Regulations

questions.prompt: The VAT on goods...

choices.text: Is a selling expense of the trader.
Is imposed on goods for domestic consumption.
It is not based on net sales.
Maybe due even if there is no actual sale of the goods.

questions.rationale: VAT may be due even without an actual sale, such as in constructive sales, deemed sales transactions (e.g., retirement from business, change of use, distribution to shareholders), or importation of goods. These transactions trigger VAT liability despite the absence of a conventional sale.
questions.canonicalConcept: Deemed sales and constructive sales triggering VAT liability without actual sale

questions.prompt: The Congregation of the Mary Immaculate donated a land and a dormitory building located along Espana Street in favor of the Sisters of the Holy Cross, a group of nuns operating a free clinic and high school teaching basic spiritual values. Is the donation subject to donor's tax?

choices.text: Yes, the donation is subject to donor's tax because the donee is a stranger.
Yes, the donation is subject to donor's tax because it failed to mention whether the donee used maximum of 30% of the amount or property donated for administrative purposes.
No, the donation is not subject to donor's tax because the donee is a non-stock, non-profit organization engaged principally for religious and educational vocation.
No, the donation is exempt from all taxes.

questions.rationale: Under Section 101(A)(3) of the NIRC, donations to non-stock, non-profit educational institutions are exempt only if not more than 30% of the gifts are used for administration. Since the facts do not mention compliance with the 30% administrative cap, the donation is subject to donor's tax.
questions.canonicalConcept: Donor's tax exemption for donations to non-stock non-profit educational institutions under Section 101(A)(3)

questions.prompt: Royal Mining is a VAT-registered domestic mining entity. One of its products is gold being sold to Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas. It filed a claim with the BIR for tax refund on the ground that under Section 106 of the NIRC, sales of precious metal to Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas are considered export sales subject to zero-rated VAT. Is Royal Mining's claim for refund meritorious?

choices.text: Yes, sale of precious gold to Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas are deemed zero-rated transactions.
Yes, sale of precious gold to Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas is deemed an export sale hence, input thereon may be credited or refunded.
No, sale of gold to Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas is exempt, hence, input is deemed expense and cannot be refunded.
No, sale of gold to Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas is vatable hence input are creditable not refundable.

questions.rationale: Although Section 106 of the NIRC treats sales of precious metals to the BSP as export sales, Revenue Regulations No. 16-2005 clarified that such sales are effectively VAT-exempt, not zero-rated. Because the sale is exempt, any input VAT paid on purchases attributable thereto cannot be refunded or credited; it is treated as an expense.
questions.canonicalConcept: VAT treatment of gold sales to Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas under RR 16-2005

questions.prompt: Congress enacts a law imposing a 5% tax on gross receipts of common carriers. The law does not define the term 'gross receipts'. Express Transport, Inc., a bus company plying the Manila-Baguio route, has time deposits with ABC Bank. In 2005, Express Transport earned P1 million interest, after deducting the 20% final withholding tax from its time deposits with the bank. The BIR wants to collect a 5% gross receipts tax on the interest income of Express Transport without deducting the 20% final withholding tax. Is the BIR correct?

choices.text: Yes, gross receipts mean cash collected whether actually or constructively without any deductions.
Yes, gross receipts mean all cash collection actually received without any deductions.
No, gross receipts mean actual receipts after deducting of withholding tax.
No, gross receipts mean actual receipts derived from business operations.

questions.rationale: Gross receipts for common carriers under the Tax Code refer to actual receipts derived from the business operations of common carriage. Interest income from time deposits is passive income subject to final withholding tax and is not derived from the common carrier's business operations; therefore, it is not part of gross receipts for percentage tax purposes.
questions.canonicalConcept: Definition of gross receipts for common carriers under the NIRC

questions.prompt: Lily's Fashion, Inc. is a garment manufacturer located and registered as a Subic Bay Freeport Enterprise under Republic Act No. 7227 and a non-VAT taxpayer. As such, it is exempt from payment of all local and national internal revenue taxes. During its operations, it purchased various supplies and materials necessary in the conduct of its manufacturing business. The suppliers of these goods shifted to Lily's Fashion, Inc. the 12% VAT on the purchased items amounting to P500,000.00. What is the proper remedy of Lily's Fashion Inc.?

choices.text: Lily's Fashion Inc., may use the P500,000 as tax credit.
Lily's Fashion Inc., may ask for a refund of the P500,000 from its supplier.
Lily's Fashion Inc., may convert the P500,000 into tax warrants.
Lily's Fashion Inc., may charge it to cost or expense.

questions.rationale: As a Subic Bay Freeport Enterprise under RA 7227, Lily's Fashion is exempt from all local and national internal revenue taxes, including VAT. When VAT is erroneously passed on by suppliers, the proper remedy is to seek a refund from the supplier because the entity cannot claim input tax credits or refunds from the BIR due to its tax-exempt status.
questions.canonicalConcept: VAT remedy for tax-exempt Subic Bay Freeport Enterprises under RA 7227

questions.prompt: A decedent died single, leaving a family home which consists of a piece of land that he inherited 3-1/2 years ago (with a value at the time of P600,000) with a fair value of P800,000 at the time of his death, and a house thereon which he built at a cost of P650,000, and a fair market value at the time of his death of P450,000. Other properties in his gross estate have a fair market value of P550,000. Unpaid obligations at the time of his death amounted to P300,000. The vanishing deduction is:
questions.rationale: The vanishing deduction is computed using the lower of the fair market value at the time of prior transfer (P600,000) or at death (P800,000). The initial basis of P600,000 is reduced by prorated deductions (P600,000 / P1,800,000 * P300,000 = P100,000), yielding P500,000. Multiplied by the 40% rate for property inherited more than 3 years but not more than 4 years prior to death, the vanishing deduction is P200,000.
questions.canonicalConcept: Vanishing deduction computation under Section 86 of the NIRC

questions.prompt: The following are non-tax incentives given to barangay micro business enterprises, except?

choices.text: Income tax exemption from all income arising from the operations of the enterprise.
Exemption from the coverage of the Minimum Wage Law (employees will still receive the same social security and health care benefits as other employees).
Priority to a special credit window set up specifically for the financing requirements of BMBEs.
Technology transfer, production and management training, and marketing assistance programs for BMBE beneficiaries.

questions.rationale: Income tax exemption is a tax incentive, not a non-tax incentive. The non-tax incentives for BMBEs under RA 9178 include exemption from the Minimum Wage Law (with preserved benefits), priority access to special credit windows, and technology transfer/training programs.
questions.canonicalConcept: BMBE incentives under RA 9178 Barangay Micro Business Enterprises Act

questions.prompt: For estate tax purposes, what are allowable deductions for nonresident alien? I. Claims, losses, indebtedness and taxes. II. Transfer for Public Use III. Property previously taxed IV. Family Home V. Standard VI. Medical Expenses VII. Amount from R.A. 4917 otherwise known as death benefits VIII. Share of the surviving spouse

choices.text: I, II, III, V and VIII
I, II, III, IV, V and VIII

questions.rationale: For nonresident aliens, allowable deductions from the gross estate include claims/losses/indebtedness/taxes, transfers for public use, property previously taxed, the standard deduction, and the share of the surviving spouse. Family home, medical expenses, and RA 4917 benefits are not allowed as deductions for nonresident aliens under Section 86 of the NIRC.
questions.canonicalConcept: Allowable deductions for nonresident alien estates under Section 86 of the NIRC

questions.prompt: For estate tax purposes, what are allowable deductions for resident citizen? I. Funeral Expenses II. Judicial Expenses III. Claims against the estate, claims against insolvent, mortgages, taxes, losses IV. Transfer for Public Use V. Property previously taxed VI. Family Home VII. Standard VIII. Medical Expenses IX. Amount from R.A. 4917 otherwise known as death benefits X. Share of the surviving spouse

choices.text: I, II, III, IV and VIII
I, II, III, IV, V and VIII
I, II, III, IV, V and VIII
III, IV, V, VI, VII, IX and X

questions.rationale: For resident citizens, all enumerated deductions are allowable under Section 86 of the NIRC, including funeral expenses, judicial expenses, claims against the estate, transfers for public use, property previously taxed, family home, standard deduction, medical expenses, RA 4917 amounts, and the share of the surviving spouse.
questions.canonicalConcept: Allowable deductions for resident citizen estates under Section 86 of the NIRC

questions.prompt: For 2025, the published price of Manang Nasal, two-piece pork barbeque stick with rice is P100.00. How much will a senior citizen pay?
questions.rationale: Under the Expanded Senior Citizens Act (RA 9994), senior citizens are entitled to a 20% discount and VAT exemption. The computation is: VAT = P100 * 12/112 = P10.71; 20% discount = (P100 - P10.71) * 20% = P17.85; Net amount = P100 - P10.71 - P17.85 = P71.44, rounded to P71.50.
questions.canonicalConcept: Senior citizen discount and VAT exemption computation under RA 9994

questions.prompt: Mang Tado owns a 4-door apartment located in Mabalacat, Pampanga. He lives in one of the apartment units and have the other units of apartment for lease. The assessed level of residential properties is 20%, agricultural properties 30% and commercial properties 50%. The fair market value of the land is P4,000,000 and house P4,000,000. How much is Mang Tado's Real Property Tax?
questions.rationale: The property is mixed-use. The portion used as residence (1/4) is assessed at residential rate: (P8,000,000 * 1/4 * 20%) * 2% = P8,000. The leased portion (3/4) is commercial: (P8,000,000 * 3/4 * 50%) * 2% = P60,000. Total RPT = P68,000.
questions.canonicalConcept: Real Property Tax computation for mixed-use property under the Local Government Code

questions.prompt: On July 31, 2025, Esperanza received a preliminary assessment notice from the BIR demanding that she pays P180,000.00 deficiency income taxes on her 2023 income. How many days from July 31, 2025 should Esperanza respond to the notice?
questions.rationale: Under the NIRC and Revenue Regulations, a taxpayer must respond to a Preliminary Assessment Notice (PAN) within 15 days from receipt. Failure to respond within this period allows the BIR to issue a Final Assessment Notice (FAN).
questions.canonicalConcept: 15-day response period for Preliminary Assessment Notice under the NIRC

questions.prompt: On March 30, 2020, Miguel Foods, Inc. received a notice of assessment and a letter of demand on its April 15, 2017 final adjustment return from the BIR. Miguel Foods then filed a request for reinvestigation together with the requisite supporting documents on April 25, 2020. On June 2, 2020, the BIR issued a final assessment reducing the amount of tax demanded. Since Miguel Foods was dissatisfied with the reduction, it did not do anything anymore. On April 15, 2025 the BIR garnished the corporation's bank deposit to answer for the tax liability. Was the BIR action proper?

choices.text: Yes. The BIR has 5 years from the filing of the protest within which to collect.
Yes. The BIR has 5 years from the issuance of the final assessment within which to collect.
No. The taxpayer did not apply for a compromise.
No. The BIR right to collect already prescribed.

questions.rationale: Under Section 222 of the NIRC, when a taxpayer files a request for reinvestigation supported by documents, the prescriptive period for collection is suspended. The BIR has 5 years from the issuance of the final assessment within which to collect the tax due.
questions.canonicalConcept: Prescriptive period for collection after reinvestigation under Section 222 of the NIRC

questions.prompt: When a BIR decision affirming an assessment is appealed to the CTA, the BIR's power to garnish the taxpayer's bank deposit...

choices.text: Is suspended to await the finality of such decision.
Is suspended given that the CTA can reverse BIR decisions when prejudicial to the taxpayer.
Is not suspended because only final decisions of the BIR are subject to appeal.
Is not suspended since the continued existence of government depends on tax collection.

questions.rationale: The BIR's power to garnish is not suspended by an appeal to the Court of Tax Appeals. Collection of taxes is not stayed pending appeal unless a valid bond or surety is posted, as the government's need for revenue is immediate and continuous under the lifeblood doctrine.
questions.canonicalConcept: Lifeblood doctrine and non-suspension of collection pending appeal to CTA

questions.prompt: Jeopardy assessment is a valid ground to compromise a tax...

choices.text: Involving deficiency income taxes only, but not for other taxes.
Because of doubt as to the validity of the assessment.
If the compromise amount does not exceed 10% of the basic tax.
Only when there is an approval of the National Investigation Division.

questions.rationale: A jeopardy assessment is a valid ground for compromise when there is doubt as to the validity of the assessment. Under the NIRC, the Commissioner may compromise tax liabilities when a reasonable doubt exists as to the taxpayer's liability or when collection costs would exceed the amount collectible.
questions.canonicalConcept: Compromise of tax liabilities based on doubt as to validity under the NIRC

questions.prompt: As a general rule, within what period must a taxpayer elevate to the Court of Tax Appeals a denial of his application for refund of income tax overpayment?

choices.text: At the taxpayer option within 30 days from receipt of the Commissioner's denial of his application for refund or lapse of 180-day decision period by CIR.
Within 30 days from receipt of the denial which must not exceed 2 years from payment of income tax.
Within 2 years from payment of income taxes sought to be refunded.
Within 30 days from receipt of the denial or within two years from payment, whichever comes first.

questions.rationale: Under the NIRC and prevailing jurisprudence (CIR v. Aichi Forging Company), a taxpayer may appeal to the Court of Tax Appeals within 30 days from receipt of the Commissioner's denial or from the lapse of the 180-day period within which the Commissioner should have acted on the claim for refund.
questions.canonicalConcept: Two-year rule and 180-day rule for tax refund appeals to the Court of Tax Appeals

questions.prompt: What is the effect on the tax liability of a taxpayer who does not protest an assessment for deficiency taxes?

choices.text: The taxpayer may appeal his liability to the CTA since the assessment is a final decision of the Commissioner on the matter.
The BIR could already enforce the collection of the taxpayer's liability if it could secure authority from the CTA.
The taxpayer's liability becomes fixed and subject to collection as the assessment becomes final and collectible.
The taxpayer's liability remains suspended for 180 days from the expiration of the period to protest.

questions.rationale: When a taxpayer fails to protest a deficiency tax assessment within the prescribed period, the assessment becomes final, executory, and demandable. The BIR may then proceed with collection remedies without further delay or need for CTA authority.
questions.canonicalConcept: Effect of failure to protest deficiency tax assessment under the NIRC

questions.prompt: There is prima facie evidence of a false or fraudulent return where the...

choices.text: Tax return was amended after a notice of assessment was issued.
Tax return was filed beyond the reglementary period.
Taxpayer changed his address without notifying the BIR.
Deductions claimed exceed by 30% the actual allowable deductions.

questions.rationale: Under Revenue Regulations, there is prima facie evidence of a false or fraudulent return when the deductions claimed exceed by 30% or more the actual allowable deductions, or when there is a substantial understatement of income.
questions.canonicalConcept: Prima facie evidence of false or fraudulent return under Revenue Regulations

questions.prompt: Patricia was injured in a vehicular accident in 2023. He incurred and paid medical expenses of P100,000 and legal fees of P50,000 during that year. In 2023, he recovered P350,000 as settlement from the insurance company which insured the car owned by the other party involved in the accident. From the above payments and transactions, the amount of income taxable to Patricia in 2023 is:
questions.rationale: Amounts received as compensation for personal injuries and sickness are excluded from gross income under Section 32(B) of the NIRC. The recovery of P350,000 compensates for the injury, and the medical and legal expenses are personal in nature and do not create taxable income. Thus, no amount is taxable to Patricia.
questions.canonicalConcept: Exclusion from gross income of amounts received for personal injuries under Section 32(B)

questions.prompt: Statement one: The CIR may issue subpoena duces tecum and failure to obey subpoena may result in criminal prosecution. Statement two: The Revenue Officer concerned must be present on the date indicated on the subpoena to determine the completeness of submission of the taxpayer.
questions.rationale: The Commissioner of Internal Revenue has the power to issue subpoena duces tecum under the NIRC, and willful disobedience may result in criminal prosecution. The Revenue Officer must be present on the indicated date to verify and determine the completeness of the taxpayer's submission.
questions.canonicalConcept: CIR subpoena powers and taxpayer compliance under the NIRC

questions.prompt: In filing a protest with the Bureau of Internal Revenue, what remedies may be availed by the taxpayer simultaneously?
questions.rationale: In filing a protest with the BIR, the taxpayer may simultaneously avail of reinvestigation or reconsideration. These are the two primary modes of administrative protest available to a taxpayer disputing an assessment.
questions.canonicalConcept: Administrative protest remedies available to taxpayers under the NIRC

questions.prompt: What is the prescriptive period for an assessment involving fraud?

choices.text: 5 years from date of the return or deadline prescribed by law whichever is later.
10 years from the date of the return or deadline prescribed by law whichever is later.

questions.rationale: For fraudulent returns or false returns with intent to evade tax, the BIR may assess taxes within 10 years from the discovery of the fraud or falsity under Section 222(a) of the NIRC. This is distinct from the ordinary 3-year prescriptive period.
questions.canonicalConcept: Prescriptive period for assessment of fraudulent returns under Section 222(a) of the NIRC

questions.prompt: The prescriptive period for tax warrant or check for refund or tax credit shall be within:
questions.rationale: Tax warrants or checks for refund or tax credit must be presented for payment within 5 years from the date of issue under the NIRC, after which they become stale and the amount reverts to the government.
questions.canonicalConcept: Prescriptive period for tax refund warrants and checks under the NIRC

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a proper way to deliver a final assessment notice?
questions.rationale: A Final Assessment Notice may be served through personal delivery, registered mail, or substituted service under Revenue Regulations. Electronic messaging alone is not a recognized mode of service for final assessments.
questions.canonicalConcept: Proper modes of service of Final Assessment Notice under Revenue Regulations

questions.prompt: How long must book of accounts be preserved?
questions.rationale: Books of accounts and other accounting records must be preserved for a period of 5 years from the date of the last entry, or as required by the BIR for audit and verification purposes under Section 235 of the NIRC.
questions.canonicalConcept: Record retention period for books of accounts under Section 235 of the NIRC

questions.prompt: For filing late return by small business enterprises, a surcharge or administrative penalty of:

choices.text: 10% shall be imposed on the basic tax.
25% shall be imposed on the basic tax.
50% shall be imposed on the basic tax.

questions.rationale: Under the NIRC, a surcharge of 25% is generally imposed for late filing. However, for small business enterprises under specific BIR regulations and amnesty provisions, a reduced surcharge of 10% may apply.
questions.canonicalConcept: Surcharge for late filing by small business enterprises under the NIRC

questions.prompt: ABC Corporation won a tax refund case for P50 Million. Upon execution of the judgment and when trying to get the Tax Credit Certificates (TCC) representing the refund, the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) refused to issue the TCC on the basis of the fact that the corporation is under audit by the BIR and it has a potential tax liability. Is there a valid justification for the BIR to withhold the issuance of the TCC?

choices.text: Yes, power of the BIR to make assessment and collection of all national internal revenue taxes, fees and charges.
Yes, power of the BIR to enforce all national taxes, fees and charges including forfeitures, penalties and fines connected therewith.
No, BIR is only in the assessment stage and not yet in the collection stage.
No, the BIR is inferior to the final and executory judgment of the court.

questions.rationale: Once a tax refund judgment becomes final and executory, the BIR cannot withhold the issuance of Tax Credit Certificates merely because the corporation is under audit or has a potential tax liability. The final judgment of the court prevails over the BIR's administrative assessment stage.
questions.canonicalConcept: Effect of final and executory judgment on tax refund claims vs BIR audit authority

questions.prompt: One of the following is NOT an inherent limitation:

choices.text: Taxes must be for public purposes.

questions.rationale: Equality in taxation is a constitutional limitation, not an inherent limitation on the power of taxation. The inherent limitations are: taxes must be for public purpose, territoriality, and international comity. Constitutional limitations include uniformity and equity in taxation.
questions.canonicalConcept: Inherent limitations vs constitutional limitations on the power of taxation

questions.prompt: A tax is invalid, EXCEPT:

choices.text: Theory of taxation and its purpose are disregarded.
Basis of taxation is not recognized.
Inherent and constitutional limitations are not observed.

questions.rationale: While double taxation is generally disfavored, it is not per se invalid unless it violates constitutional or statutory provisions. A tax may be invalid if it disregards the theory and purpose of taxation, lacks a recognized basis, or violates inherent or constitutional limitations.
questions.canonicalConcept: Validity of taxes and the concept of double taxation under Philippine tax law

questions.prompt: The government may not do all, except one:

choices.text: Delegate its power to tax to private agencies.

questions.rationale: The government may tax itself in certain instances where immunity is waived. However, the government cannot delegate its taxing power to private agencies, impose taxes arbitrarily, or disregard uniformity in taxation.
questions.canonicalConcept: Government powers and limitations in taxation under the Philippine Constitution

questions.prompt: Gerry Llamanzares, married, resident citizen, is in the business of leasing real properties. In 2026, he had rental income from real property net of 5% withholding tax of P285,000 (real property tax paid by lessor P50,000, lessee reimbursed 50%, deductible expense P120,000) and rental income net of 5% withholding tax of P142,500 (real property tax P20,000, lessee reimbursed 100%, deductible expense P40,000). Determine the operational net income of Gerry.
questions.rationale: Gross receipts: Rental 1 gross = P285,000 / 0.95 = P300,000 plus RPT reimbursed P25,000 = P325,000. Rental 2 gross = P142,500 / 0.95 = P150,000 plus RPT reimbursed P20,000 = P170,000. Total gross receipts P495,000. Less itemized deductions: expenses P160,000 + RPT paid to LGU P70,000 = P230,000. Net income from operations = P265,000.
questions.canonicalConcept: Operational net income computation for lessor with reimbursed real property taxes

questions.prompt: Using the same facts about Gerry Llamanzares, he also sold shares of ABC (domestic, not traded) for P300,000 (cost P180,000), shares of DEF (domestic, traded in NYSE) for P100,000 (cost P150,000), shares of XYZ (foreign, traded in NYSE) for P500,000 (cost P100,000), a vacant lot in the Philippines for P800,000 (cost P200,000), and a Toyota car for family use for P100,000 (cost P300,000). He also had worthless shares of Alpha Corporation (cost P50,000) and a liquidating dividend from Beta Corporation of P450,000 (investment in 2000 was P375,000). Determine the Net Capital Gains in Gerry's 2026 AITR.
questions.rationale: Capital gains included in the AITR: foreign shares sold through a foreign stock exchange (gain P200,000) and liquidating dividend gain (P75,000), totaling P275,000. Capital losses: family car loss (P100,000) and worthless shares (P25,000), totaling P125,000. Net capital gain = P150,000. Note that shares of ABC (not traded) and the vacant lot are subject to final taxes and excluded from the AITR; shares of DEF traded in NYSE are subject to stock transaction tax.
questions.canonicalConcept: Net capital gains computation for AITR excluding assets subject to final taxes and stock transaction tax

questions.prompt: Determine the net taxable income of Gerry in his 2026 AITR.
questions.rationale: Net taxable income is computed as net income from operations (P265,000) plus net capital gains included in the AITR (P150,000), totaling P415,000. Assets subject to final taxes (shares of ABC, vacant lot) and stock transaction tax (shares of DEF) are excluded from the AITR computation.
questions.canonicalConcept: Net taxable income computation combining operational income and net capital gains in the AITR

questions.prompt: Atty. Dehado, resident citizen, married, died leaving real properties with the following FMVs at the time of death in 2025: Commercial building P40,000,000, Residential property P25,000,000, Family Home P28,000,000. The commercial building and residential property were acquired during marriage. The family home was inherited from his parents before he got married. If Atty. Dehado got married in 1987, how much of the value of the family home would be subject to Philippine estate tax?
questions.rationale: For marriages before the effectivity of the Family Code (August 3, 1988), the conjugal partnership of gains applies. The family home inherited before marriage is exclusive property. The family home deduction is limited to P10,000,000 under the NIRC. Therefore, the amount subject to estate tax is P28,000,000 - P10,000,000 = P18,000,000.
questions.canonicalConcept: Family home deduction for marriages before the Family Code under the NIRC estate tax rules

questions.prompt: If Atty. Dehado got married in 1989, how much of the value of the family home would be subject to Philippine estate tax?
questions.rationale: For marriages after the Family Code, the absolute community of property applies. The family home inherited before marriage remains exclusive property. After applying the family home deduction of P10,000,000 and considering the spouse's share in the absolute community, the taxable portion of the family home is P4,000,000.
questions.canonicalConcept: Family home deduction for marriages after the Family Code under the NIRC estate tax rules

questions.prompt: Spouses Albert and Belen Gayeta donated a mango orchard to their sons, Willy and Wally. Since Willy was busy with his medical practice, the brothers agreed that Wally will have possession and administration of the orchard, with the net harvest divided equally between them. Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.text: Willy and Wally are partners, and will report their respective shares in the net harvest as part of taxable income in their respective ITRs.
Willy and Wally are not partners, but will report their respective shares in the net harvest as part of taxable income in their respective ITRs.
Willy and Wally are partners, and their respective shares in the net harvest will be subject to final taxes.
Willy and Wally are not partners, hence their respective shares in the net harvest are not subject to tax.

questions.rationale: Co-ownership of property does not automatically create a partnership. Where brothers merely divide the net harvest from co-owned property without creating a partnership for business purposes, they are co-owners, not partners. Each must report his share of the income in his individual income tax return.
questions.canonicalConcept: Co-ownership income reporting vs partnership taxation under the NIRC

questions.prompt: Interest income from outside the Philippines earned by a resident alien is...

choices.text: Partly subject to schedular and partly subject to final tax.

questions.rationale: A resident alien is taxed only on income derived from sources within the Philippines under Section 23 of the NIRC. Interest income from outside the Philippines is foreign-sourced income and is not subject to Philippine income tax for resident aliens.
questions.canonicalConcept: Taxation of foreign-sourced interest income for resident aliens under Section 23 of the NIRC

questions.prompt: The following sales or transactions by VAT-registered persons/entities shall be 0-rated except:

choices.text: Sales of goods/services to an export-oriented enterprise whose export sales is at least 75% of its total annual production of the preceding taxable year.
Transport of passengers/cargo by domestic carriers from the Philippines to a foreign country.
Sale of raw materials, inventories, supplies, equipment, packaging materials, and goods to RBEs which are qualified for VAT 0-rating on their purchases under Title XIII of the Tax Code.
Sale of power or fuel generated through renewable sources of energy such as solar, wind, biomass, geothermal, and ocean energy.

questions.rationale: Sales to export-oriented enterprises are zero-rated only if export sales constitute at least 70% (not 75%) of total annual production of the preceding taxable year. The 75% threshold stated in the option is incorrect and therefore does not qualify for zero-rating.
questions.canonicalConcept: Zero-rated VAT threshold for sales to export-oriented enterprises under the NIRC

questions.prompt: Dynamite Corporation, a domestic corporation, took 2 life insurance policies on the life of its dynamic manager. The first policy's designated beneficiary is Dynamite Corporation while the second policy's designated beneficiary is his wife, Sarah. The insurance premiums paid by Dynamite are:

choices.text: Deductible, only in so far as the first policy is concerned.
Deductible in so far as the second policy is concerned.

questions.rationale: Life insurance premiums paid by a corporation are deductible if the beneficiary is an officer, employee, or their estate or heirs (second policy - wife). Premiums are not deductible if the corporation is the beneficiary (first policy) as this constitutes an indirect distribution of capital.
questions.canonicalConcept: Deductibility of life insurance premiums based on beneficiary designation under the NIRC

questions.prompt: Any VAT-registered person, whose sales are 0-rated, may apply for the issuance of a tax credit certificate or refund of input taxes on purchases attributable to 0-rated sales within:

choices.text: 2 years after the close of the taxable year.
5 years after the close of the taxable year.
2 years after the close of the taxable quarter.
5 years after the close of the taxable quarter.

questions.rationale: Under Section 112 of the NIRC, a VAT-registered person with zero-rated sales may apply for a tax credit certificate or refund of input taxes within 2 years after the close of the taxable quarter when the zero-rated sales were made.
questions.canonicalConcept: Two-year period for VAT refund application on zero-rated sales under Section 112 of the NIRC

questions.prompt: Statement 1: The excise tax shall apply to all goods manufactured/produced in the Philippines, and to all things imported. Statement 2: The excise tax imposed shall be in lieu of the VAT.
questions.rationale: Excise tax does not apply to all goods but only to specific goods listed in the NIRC (alcohol, tobacco, petroleum, automobiles, mineral products, sweetened beverages). It is also not in lieu of VAT but is imposed in addition to VAT.
questions.canonicalConcept: Scope of excise tax and its relationship with VAT under the NIRC

questions.prompt: Statement 1: Before January 1, 2022, if the aggregate cost of the capital goods purchased in a calendar month exceeded P1.0 Million, the input VAT was required to be amortized over the life of the capital good or 5 years, whichever was shorter. Statement 2: Senior citizens and PWDs are exempt from VAT on all their purchases of goods and services.
questions.rationale: Before January 1, 2022, input VAT on capital goods exceeding P1 million in a calendar month was indeed amortized over the useful life or 5 years, whichever is shorter. However, senior citizens and PWDs are exempt from VAT only on specific goods and services, not on all purchases.
questions.canonicalConcept: Input VAT amortization rules and senior citizen VAT exemptions under the NIRC

questions.prompt: KingArum Enterprises, a domestic corporation, 60% Filipino-owned, had the following gross receipts from world championship events in the Philippines: Billiards P1,000,000; Tennis P2,000,000; Basketball P3,000,000; Volleyball P4,000,000; Boxing P10,000,000. The OPT due is:
questions.rationale: Under the NIRC and relevant regulations, world championship events featuring international athletes are exempt from the amusement tax and other percentage taxes if they meet specific criteria for international competitions. The OPT due is zero.
questions.canonicalConcept: Exemption from amusement tax and OPT for international sports competitions under the NIRC

questions.prompt: Which of the following importations is subject to VAT?
questions.rationale: Importation of abaca and cotton is subject to VAT, whereas rice, corn, coffee beans, and lamb/goat meat are specifically exempt from VAT under the NIRC as agricultural products in their raw state.
questions.canonicalConcept: VAT-exempt importations of agricultural products under the NIRC

questions.prompt: Which of the following importations is subject to VAT?
questions.rationale: Vegetable oil is subject to VAT upon importation. Ordinary salt, copra, and husked rice are agricultural products that are exempt from VAT under the NIRC.
questions.canonicalConcept: VAT treatment of imported agricultural and food products under the NIRC

questions.prompt: A resident citizen received a prize of P40,000. Which of the following statements is correct in connection with the imposition of final tax on prize?

choices.text: The first P10,000 is part of taxable income while the remaining P30,000 is subject to 20% final tax.
The whole amount is part of taxable income.
The whole amount of P40,000 shall be subject to a 20% final tax.
The first P10,000 shall be exempt from tax, the remaining P30,000 is subject to a 20% final tax.

questions.rationale: Under Section 24(B) of the NIRC, prizes exceeding P10,000 are subject to a 20% final tax on the entire amount. The first P10,000 exemption applies only to winnings and prizes from PCSO/Lotto. For other prizes, the full amount is subject to final tax if it exceeds P10,000.
questions.canonicalConcept: Final tax on prizes exceeding P10,000 under Section 24(B) of the NIRC

questions.prompt: A domestic proprietary educational institution improved its library and computer room. For income tax purposes, the amounts spent for such improvements may be:

choices.text: Deducted in full at the time of completion of the improvement.
Capitalized or expensed outright at the option of the school owner.
Capitalized and depreciated over the estimated life of the improvement.
Capitalized or expensed outright at the option of the government.

questions.rationale: For proprietary educational institutions, amounts spent for improvements may be capitalized and depreciated or expensed outright at the option of the school owner, provided the method is consistently applied.
questions.canonicalConcept: Tax treatment of improvements by proprietary educational institutions under the NIRC

questions.prompt: In our jurisdiction, which of the following statements may be erroneous?

choices.text: Taxes are enforced charges and contributions.
Taxes are imposed on persons and property within the territorial jurisdiction of a State.
Taxes are levied and collected by the legislative branch of the government.

questions.rationale: Taxes are levied by the legislative branch (Congress) but are collected by the executive branch (BIR, Bureau of Customs). The statement that taxes are levied and collected by the legislative branch is erroneous.
questions.canonicalConcept: Nature of taxes and the separation of legislative and executive functions in taxation

questions.prompt: Albert de Vera bought a condominium unit under installment basis, to be used as his office in the practice of his profession and is paying P10,000 monthly. For income tax purposes, the P10,000 monthly payment shall be:

choices.text: Treated as business rental, hence deductible.
Treated as depreciation expense, hence deductible.
Treated as capital expenditure, hence not deductible.

questions.rationale: Installment payments for the acquisition of a condominium unit to be used as an office constitute capital expenditures. The cost must be capitalized and depreciated over the useful life of the property; it cannot be deducted as a current rental or ordinary expense.
questions.canonicalConcept: Capital expenditure vs deductible expense for installment purchase of business property

questions.prompt: Hilario Esteban, Filipino, married Wendy Santos in 2004. He died on August 13, 2024. The estate reported conjugal properties: Fishpond Pampanga P2,000,000; Apartment houses Quezon City P1,000,000; Cash in bank P800,000; Family home P30,000,000. Exclusive properties of Hilario: Land inherited from father (value when inherited P210,000, mortgage P30,000 of which P10,000 was paid) FMV P400,000; Land donated by mother (value when donated P500,000) FMV P600,000. Exclusive property of Wendy: Farm donated by mother 10 days after wedding P3,000,000. Deductions claimed: Funeral P250,000; Fire loss P80,000; Bad debt P100,000; Mortgage on inherited land P30,000; Vanishing deduction inherited land P75,000; Vanishing deduction donated land P90,000; Standard deduction P1,000,000. Determine the gross estate of Hilario.
questions.rationale: Gross estate includes conjugal properties (fishpond P2M + apartment P1M + cash P800K + family home P30M = P33.8M) plus exclusive properties of the decedent (inherited land P400K + donated land P600K = P1M), totaling P34.9M. The farm donated to Wendy is her exclusive property and not part of the decedent's gross estate.
questions.canonicalConcept: Gross estate computation including conjugal and exclusive properties under the NIRC

questions.prompt: Using the same facts about Hilario Esteban, what is the total amount of proper deductions chargeable against the conjugal properties of the estate?
questions.rationale: Deductions chargeable against conjugal properties include the bad debt (P100,000) and fire loss (P80,000), totaling P180,000. Funeral expenses and standard deduction are allocated proportionally between conjugal and exclusive properties.
questions.canonicalConcept: Allocation of deductions between conjugal and exclusive properties in estate tax

questions.prompt: Using the same facts about Hilario Esteban, what is the total amount of proper deductions chargeable against the exclusive properties of the estate?
questions.rationale: Deductions chargeable against exclusive properties include the prorated unpaid mortgage on inherited land (P20,000), vanishing deductions (P159,083 + P99,427 = P258,510), and other prorated ordinary deductions allocated to exclusive properties, totaling approximately P278,510.
questions.canonicalConcept: Deductions chargeable against exclusive properties including vanishing deductions

questions.prompt: Using the same facts about Hilario Esteban, compute the net taxable estate.
questions.rationale: Gross estate P34.9M less ordinary deductions (P200,000 + vanishing deductions P258,510) = P34,441,490. Less special deductions: family home P10M, standard deduction P5M, net share of surviving spouse (1/2 of P33.72M conjugal net) P16,860,000. Net estate subject to tax = P2,581,490.
questions.canonicalConcept: Net taxable estate computation with special deductions and surviving spouse share

questions.prompt: Using the same facts about Hilario Esteban, compute the estate tax due.
questions.rationale: Net estate of P2,581,490 multiplied by the 6% estate tax rate under the TRAIN Law equals P154,889.40, rounded to P154,889.
questions.canonicalConcept: Estate tax due computation at 6% rate under the TRAIN Law

questions.prompt: Using the same facts about Hilario Esteban, compute the total estate tax plus penalties (without compromise penalties) if the estate tax was paid only on August 13, 2028.
questions.rationale: Estate tax P154,889 plus 25% surcharge P38,722 plus interest at 12% per annum for 3 years (August 13, 2025 to August 13, 2028) P55,760 equals P249,371, rounded to P249,372.
questions.canonicalConcept: Estate tax penalties including surcharge and interest under the NIRC

questions.prompt: Fuhrer Eichmann, non-resident German, married, died on April 6, 2026. The estate reported a total worldwide gross estate of P5,000,000 which includes a Philippine gross estate of P2,500,000. The estate is claiming deductions: Liabilities P450,000 (notarized); Hospitalization expenses P230,000 (incurred 5 months before death); Miscellaneous expenses P320,000 (unsupported). Determine the taxable net estate of Fuhrer Eichmann.
questions.rationale: Philippine gross estate P2.5M. Less prorated liabilities (P2.5M/P5M * P450,000 = P225,000). Net estate before special deductions = P2,275,000. Less standard deduction P500,000 and net share of surviving spouse (1/2 * P2,275,000 = P1,137,500). Net taxable estate = P637,500. Hospitalization and miscellaneous expenses are not deductible for nonresident aliens.
questions.canonicalConcept: Taxable net estate of nonresident alien with prorated deductions under the NIRC

questions.prompt: Using the same facts about Fuhrer Eichmann, determine the estate tax due.
questions.rationale: Net taxable estate of P637,500 multiplied by the 6% estate tax rate under the TRAIN Law equals P38,250.
questions.canonicalConcept: Estate tax due for nonresident alien at 6% rate under the TRAIN Law

questions.prompt: Allan Cuevas, a non-VAT registered taxpayer, started his business on February 14, 2025. For taxable year 2025, he had cumulative sales: Feb 14 to Sep 30 P1,800,000; Oct 1 to Oct 31 P2,200,000; Nov 1 to Nov 30 P2,500,000; Dec 1 to Dec 31 P3,000,000. Allan decided to register his business under the VAT system on November 5, 2025. At what month will Allan begin to be liable for VAT?
questions.rationale: Allan registered under VAT on November 5, 2025. A taxpayer who registers voluntarily becomes liable for VAT from the month of registration. Therefore, VAT liability begins in November 2025.
questions.canonicalConcept: VAT liability commencement upon voluntary registration under the NIRC

questions.prompt: Using the same facts about Allan Cuevas, for the month of October 2025, Allan will pay:
questions.rationale: For October 2025, Allan was still a non-VAT taxpayer. His sales for October were P400,000 (cumulative P2.2M less previous P1.8M). As a non-VAT taxpayer with gross receipts not yet exceeding P3M annually at that point, he is subject to 3% percentage tax (OPT) on monthly sales: P400,000 * 3% = P12,000.
questions.canonicalConcept: Percentage tax computation for non-VAT taxpayers under the NIRC

questions.prompt: Using the same facts about Allan Cuevas, for the quarter ending December 31, 2025, Allan will pay:
questions.rationale: For the quarter ending December 31, 2025, Allan is a VAT taxpayer. Output VAT: November sales P300,000 * 12% = P36,000; December sales P500,000 * 12% = P60,000. Total output VAT P96,000. Input VAT: November P25,000 + December P50,000 = P75,000. Net VAT payable = P96,000 - P75,000 = P21,000. October is under OPT, not VAT.
questions.canonicalConcept: Quarterly VAT computation for taxpayer transitioning from non-VAT to VAT status

questions.prompt: Braullo Enterprises, Inc., a VAT-registered domestic corporation, had the following during the 2nd quarter of 2026: Export Sales of Sardines $460,000 (input VAT P53,000); Vegetables EUR 500,000 (input VAT P40,000); Refined sugar GBP 650,000 (input VAT P35,000). Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.text: Only the sales of sardines shall be subject to VAT.
The sale of vegetables is exempt from VAT.
All sales are subject to 0% VAT.
The attributable input VAT can only be claimed as an expense in the ITR.

questions.rationale: Export sales of registered export-oriented enterprises are subject to 0% VAT under Section 106(A)(2) of the NIRC. This includes sardines, vegetables, and refined sugar sold for export. The attributable input VAT can be claimed as a refund or tax credit, not merely as an expense.
questions.canonicalConcept: Zero-rated VAT on export sales and treatment of input VAT under the NIRC

questions.prompt: Donor Martin Romualdo gave the following donations in 2025: On April 12, to Mike (legitimate child), a lot with unpaid mortgage of P30,000 assumed by Mike, FMV P600,000; and to the campaign of politician Zaldy P500,000 (only P250,000 used). Compute the donor's tax and the donor's tax payable on the donations made on April 12, 2025.
questions.rationale: Current gross gift P850,000 (lot P600,000 + campaign P250,000) less mortgage assumed by donee (P30,000) equals P820,000. Less exemption of P250,000, net gift subject to tax is P570,000. Donor's tax at 6% = P34,200. Since this is the first donation, tax payable equals tax due.
questions.canonicalConcept: Donor's tax computation on mixed donations including political campaign contributions

questions.prompt: On June 6, 2025, Martin Romualdo gave P20,000 to Bruno (brother) on account of marriage on October 8, 2025. Compute the donor's tax and the donor's tax payable on the donations made on June 6, 2025.
questions.rationale: Current gross gift P20,000. Add prior net gifts P820,000. Total net gifts P840,000. Less exemption P250,000. Net gifts subject to tax P590,000. Tax at 6% = P35,400. Less prior tax paid P34,200. Tax payable = P1,200.
questions.canonicalConcept: Cumulative donor's tax computation with prior net gifts under the NIRC

questions.prompt: On July 30, 2025, Martin Romualdo gave P40,000 to Yolo (brother-in-law). Compute the donor's tax and the donor's tax payable on the donations made on July 30, 2025.
questions.rationale: Current gross gift P40,000. Add prior net gifts P840,000. Total P880,000. Less exemption P250,000. Net subject to tax P630,000. Tax at 6% = P37,800. Less prior tax paid P35,400. Tax payable = P2,400.
questions.canonicalConcept: Cumulative donor's tax computation for donation to stranger under the NIRC

questions.prompt: On November 24, 2025, Martin Romualdo gave P10,000 to Xanadu (legitimate child) as birthday gift and P50,000 to the Philippine National Red Cross. Compute the donor's tax and the donor's tax payable on the donations made on November 24, 2025.
questions.rationale: Current gross gifts P60,000. Less deduction for gift to accredited NGO (PNRC) P50,000. Current net gift P10,000. Add prior net gifts P880,000. Total P890,000. Less exemption P250,000. Net subject to tax P640,000. Tax at 6% = P38,400. Less prior tax paid P37,800. Tax payable = P600.
questions.canonicalConcept: Cumulative donor's tax computation with deduction for donation to accredited NGO under the NIRC
